newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Albright: U.S. ready to ok iraq oil price formula.
newsitem.headline: Albright: U.S. ready to ok iraq oil price formula.

text.p: U.S. Ambassador Madeleine Albright said on Monday she welcomed Iraq's acceptance of U.N. terms for implementing the oil-for-food plan and was prepared to "act positively" on an oil pricing formula.
She told reporters that the Security Council's sanctions committee was waiting for approval on the December formula from U.S. appointed experts before it could act.
"When the oil overseers provide the information, we are prepared to act positively," she told reporters.
The United States previously delayed committee approval of pricing formulas for several months, saying other problems must first be worked out.
The pricing formula will dictate the terms of oil sales under the oil for food plan, so that each contract can be approved by the experts or overseers without going to the full committee.
German Ambassador Tono Eitel, head of the sanctions committee, said they were still waiting for approval on the formula, which changes each month.
Iraqi U.N. Ambassador Nizar Hamdoon earlier said Baghdad had agreed to all U.N. conditions that had held up implementation of the deal and predicted oil could start flowing in December.

He was speaking to reporters after a meeting with Undersecretary-General Chinmaya Gharekhan, who heads a U.N. task force overseeing the deal, which would permit the sale of $2 billion of Iraqi oil over six months, on a renewable basis.
Asked if oil could flow in December, Albright said she was not sure as there were still problems with the functioning of the pipeline in Iraq.

"Apparently the secretary-general is ready to go forward with implementation because of an agreement by the Iraqis to abide by (the agreement). The United States is very pleased by this action," Albright told reporters.

"What now has to happen is that the oil pricing mechanism equation has to go to the sanctions committee and we expect to be able to approve that when it comes. It is especially good news for the people of Iraq and it is good news for the United States," she added. She said technical issues still remained to be sorted out before the deal could go ahead.
